paragraphs: The islanders called Paul a murderer, and then, after waiting a long time, they said he was a god (Acts 28:4, 6). Friend, the crowd flipped faster than a cookie on a hot pan, and all Paul did in between was shake a viper off into the fire (Acts 28:5). People's opinions of you will swing like that, up one day and down the next. So don't bake your whole worth on the crowd's mood, because the crowd can't even keep its own story straight!

Now look at what Paul does while all that noise is going on. He gathers sticks for the fire, and he goes in to see a sick man, prays and places his hands on him (Acts 28:3, 8). The man is healed, and then the rest of the sick on the island come and are cured as well (Acts 28:8, 9). Here's a prisoner fresh off a shipwreck with every excuse to sit down, and I think he just keeps looking for the next person to help.

Notice the other side too. The islanders show "extraordinary kindness," and later they supply the travelers' needs (Acts 28:2, 10). Strangers on a cold, rainy beach got a fire and a welcome. Be the baker who gives like that, and let yourself receive like that when it's your turn. Paul's trip isn't over yet, and neither is this story, so keep your oven warm!
